issues.legal_issue: A rent-control revisional court cannot reappreciate evidence and replace concurrent findings of the lower courts with its own conclusion, even when the findings concern the existence of a landlord-tenant relationship.
material_facts: The predecessor of the respondents had earlier claimed that he was a tenant, but the Land Tribunal rejected that claim and found from the owner’s accounts that he was only a manager of the theatre.
The Rent Control Court found that the respondents’ predecessor had accepted the appellants’ predecessor as landlord and ordered eviction; the Rent Control Appellate Authority affirmed that decision.
The High Court reversed the concurrent decisions after reassessing the evidence and concluding that a landlord-tenant relationship had not been established.
The Supreme Court found that the lower courts’ findings were supported by evidence and were not perverse.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its revisional jurisdiction by reappreciating the evidence. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the eviction decree affirmed by the Rent Control Appellate Authority was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 20 of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, revisional jurisdiction, though wider than the jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, does not permit the High Court to act as a first or second appellate court or to reappreciate evidence and substitute its conclusion for that of the appellate authority. The revisional court’s consideration is confined to the legality, regularity and propriety of the impugned order. This applies even when the issue is a jurisdictional fact, such as whether a landlord-tenant relationship exists. The Court relied on Rukmini Amma Saradamma v. Kallyani Sulochana, Ubaiba v. Damodaran, and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited v. Dilbahar Singh.

rule.if: rent_control_revision_case and concurrent_lower_court_findings and findings_supported_and_not_perverse and revisional_court_reappreciated_evidence

predicates.rent_control_revision_case: The proceeding before the High Court was a revision concerning a rent-control decision.
predicates.concurrent_lower_court_findings: The trial-level court and the appellate authority reached the same findings.
predicates.findings_supported_and_not_perverse: The findings of the lower courts were supported by evidence and were not perverse.
predicates.revisional_court_reappreciated_evidence: The revisional court reassessed the evidence and substituted its conclusion for the concurrent findings below.
predicates.concurrent_lower_court_decision_restored: The concurrent decision of the lower courts is restored.

issues.definition: When a revisional court in a rent-control case reassesses evidence to replace concurrent lower-court findings that are supported and not perverse, the concurrent lower-court decision is restored.
